newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Softline makes cautious debut on JSE.
newsitem.headline: Softline makes cautious debut on JSE.

text.p: South African information technology firm Softline Ltd made a cautious debut on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Wednesday despite issuing a statement that it is involved in talks with another firm.
Softline reverse listed into Benoni Gold Holdings Ltd cash shell and issued a cautionary statement saying it was engaged in negotiations which could have an effect on its share price.
"It has not come in well at all. It listed with a cautionery to prop up its price...Stand-alone it is very expensive," one dealer said.
Softline was the fourth most actively traded share on the exchange, with the share price touching a high of 270 cents before settling at 240 cents -- Benoni's closing price on Tuesday -- by 0955 GMT.
Over 264,000 shares were traded valued at 675,648 rand.
Softline said turnover for the year to February this year was expected to reach 155 million rand and sales for the next financial year were seen growing by 29 percent to 200 million rand.
It said earnings per share for this period were forecast at four cents increasing to six cents for the year to February next year.
Dealers said investors were not impressed with its earnings forecast.
"People are not completely convinced. There is not a lot of interest with volumes only a quarter of a million," one said.
The group said it was well positioned in key markets while its software development, PC retail networking and service companies offered good long term prospects for growth.
